digest.component_or_area: review-bot reconciler and retrigger handlers (/rerun, recheck-review)
propositions: Accepted /rerun and recheck-review requests enqueue forced events only to the process-local asyncio queue with no durable state; if the process exits before dequeue, the request is lost and reconciliation skips the revision because Gerrit still carries the old vote and SQLite carries stale dedup rows.

The approved repair resets the exact revision to neutral LLM-Review:0, verifies all accounts have no nonzero vote, then enqueues the forced event; the reset-emitted Gerrit comment-added event becomes the durable marker across process loss.

Reconciliation must query Gerrit before checking local dedup; if no nonzero vote is confirmed, it clears the exact stale voted row and proceeds to review; if Gerrit read fails, it preserves dedup and holds the cursor back for retry.

Contributor text in recheck-review and /rerun cannot select a label value or trigger PASS/BLOCK; only the privileged bot account posts the fixed neutral reset, and affirmative/refusal replies remain label-free.

A production Gerrit events-log probe on 2026-08-09 found 551 LLM-Review approval events; all were comment-added events carrying both patchSet.revision and patchSet.ref, confirming that a review-label write emits the fresh patchset-bearing event needed to re-admit old change revisions after a persisted reconcile cursor.

Accepted requests must reset votes and verify clean state before acknowledging; a surviving concurrent or admin nonzero vote causes failure and rejection, as the bot can reset only its own account's vote and therefore cannot establish a durable acceptance marker.
